table.sentence: He sat at the table to eat.

tackle.definition: If you tackle a problem, issue, question, etc., you try to solve it.

tail.definition: A tail is a long, thin part on the back end of an animal.

take.definition: If you take an action, you do it.
take.sentence: I'm going to take a rest. = I'm going to rest.

tale.definition: A tale is a type of story.
tale.sentence: Have you read the tale of three pigs?

talent.definition: If you have a talent in doing something, you have the skill and ability to do that task.
talent.sentence: He has got the talent in music, but his family is too poor to provide him with the proper education.

talk.definition: To speak; any sound from a person's mouth.

tall.definition: If something is tall, there is a long distance from the bottom to the top.
tall.sentence: The man was so tall that he hit his head coming in the door.

tank.definition: A tank is a large, strong container for gas or liquid.
tank.sentence: The gas stove was connected to a propane tank.

tap.definition: A device that liquids come out of.
tap.sentence: We don't have bottled water, you'll have to get it from the tap.

tape.definition: Tape is a long thin material, often with glue on one side or used for recording.
tape.sentence: We can fix the tear with some tape.

task.definition: A task is a specific piece of work, often unpleasant.
task.sentence: Come here, young man. I have a task for you to do.

taste.definition: Taste is the sense linked to the tongue, usually when eating food. The taste is how people can enjoy their food.
taste.sentence: Wow, these chicken wings taste really good, I want some more!.

taxi.definition: A taxi is a vehicle (usually a car) driven by a taxi driver; the taxi driver drives you somewhere if you pay them money.

tea.definition: Tea is a light brown or green drink that is very popular around the world.
tea.sentence: Would you like coffee or tea?

teach.definition: To help someone learn something. To tell someone how to do something.
teach.sentence: Most parents try to teach their children to be nice.

teacher.definition: A teacher is a person who teaches other people.
teacher.sentence: She was a very good teacher, I learned a lot from her.

team.definition: A team is a group of people who play or work together on the same side.
team.sentence: She is a member of the coaching team which led Great Britain to victory over Australia at last year's games.

tear.definition: A tear is hole made by pulling or ripping something.
tear.sentence: I cannot wear a shirt with a tear in it!

technical.definition: Technical problems, writing, or skills, are related to special knowledge that most people don't have.
technical.sentence: Doctors use a lot of technical vocabulary. I wish they would explain things more easily.

technique.definition: A technique is a specialized and skillful way of doing something.
technique.sentence: It is important for pilots to be taught the right technique for the take-off run.

technology.definition: Technology is the tools, equipment, and activities that come from scientific knowledge.
technology.sentence: The mastery of fire was a huge advance in human technology.

teenager.definition: A teenager is a person whose age is a number that ends in "-teen." That is, someone between the ages of 13 and 19.

telephone.definition: A machine used to talk to someone who is far away.
telephone.sentence: I need to find a telephone so I can tell my mother where I am.

television.definition: A television is a box that moving pictures can be watched on.
television.sentence: Television is a medium because it is neither rare nor well done.

tell.definition: When you tell something to someone, you speak to the person about some fact or idea.

temperature.definition: The temperature of something is how hot or cold it is.

temporary.definition: Something is temporary if it's only for a short time.
temporary.sentence: A tent was our temporary home after our house burned down in the fire.

tend.definition: To tend to do something means inclined or likely to do something.
tend.sentence: The streets are very confusing in Tokyo and people tend to get lost.

tendency.definition: A tendency is an inclination of something to behave in a particular way or to go in a particular direction.
tendency.sentence: He has a tendency to talk too much.

tennis.definition: Tennis is a sport where players use a racquet to hit a ball over a net. It can be played by two or four people.
tennis.sentence: The four girls spent the afternoon playing tennis.

tension.sentence: No one said anything, but I could feel the tension in the room.

tent.definition: A tent is similar to a house or building that is made of cloth or skins.
tent.sentence: We slept in a tent all week.

term.definition: A term is a word or group of words, usually one with a special meaning in a particular field or area.
term.sentence: What is the definition of this term?

terrible.definition: If something is terrible, it's very bad.
terrible.sentence: The witch laid a terrible curse on him.

territory.definition: A person's, animal's, or group's territory is land he, she, or they claim, own, or control.

test.definition: A test is writing that many learners do in a room at the same time so that people are able to see how much knowledge the learners have.
test.sentence: I'm happy because I got a high mark on the test.

text.sentence: The text is OK, but we need to change the graphics before we publish.

thank.definition: To say a good word after someone gives something to you or after someone does something good for you.

theater.definition: A theater is a building with a big room with a stage and places for many people to sit, so that people can watch a play with actors in it.
theater.sentence: We went to the theater to watch a play by Shakespeare.

theme.definition: A theme is a general idea that runs through a conversation, story, group of images, piece of music, etc.
theme.sentence: For Mr Giuliani, crime is a main campaign theme.

then.definition: Subsequently or soon afterward (often used as sentence connectors)

theoretical.definition: Theoretical is about theory rather than its practical application.
theoretical.sentence: Entanglement is important but difficult to study, both in terms of a theoretical understanding and doing experiments.

theory.definition: A theory is an idea that tries to explain an observation.
theory.sentence: The new information showed that his theory about growth was incorrect.

therapy.definition: Therapy is the treatment of impairment, injury, disease, or disorder.
therapy.sentence: My grandfather's therapy will start at the hospital at noon tomorrow.

there.definition: : This short section needs someone to add to it.

thick.definition: If something is thick, there is some distance from one side to the other.
thick.sentence: He was a workman with big hands and thick fingers.

thin.definition: If something is thin, there's a short distance from one side to the other.
thin.sentence: I can hear the people in the other room because the wall is thin.

thing.sentence: This thing has got to end.

think.definition: If you think that something is or may be true, you feel that it is or may be true.
think.sentence: I think the best thing to do now is to go home.

thirst.definition: Thirst is the feeling that you want to drink.
thirst.sentence: She took a long drink to ease her thirst.

threat.definition: A threat is something or someone that might be bad or dangerous, or cause a problem.
threat.sentence: The product posed a serious health threat and should not be used.

threaten.definition: To make a threat against someone; to say that you are going to do something harmful to that person.

throat.definition: Your throat is a tube inside your neck. It takes air from your mouth to your lungs.
throat.sentence: My throat hurts from singing too much.

throw.definition: When you throw an object, you make it fly through the air using your hands.
throw.sentence: Jim can throw a ball over his house.

thus.sentence: I didn't do my homework and thus got a bad grade.

ticket.definition: A ticket is a piece of paper that allows you to enter a train, airplane, show, etc.
ticket.sentence: I bought my ticket to Mexico last week, but now I can't find it.

tie.definition: If you tie something, you attach it using string or rope.
tie.sentence: I was six when I learned to tie up my shoes.

tight.definition: If x is tight, it fits closely and strongly to y.
tight.sentence: The bandage on your finger should not be too tight or your finger may turn blue.

till.definition: To make the earth ready for seeds.

time.definition: Time is what we measure with a clock.
time.sentence: I don't have time to talk to you right now. Can we do it later?

tiny.definition: Something that is tiny is very small.
tiny.sentence: A single grain of sand is tiny.

tip.definition: The tip of something is the farthest point of it.
tip.sentence: She runs her finger down the bird's back and to the tip of its tail.

tire.definition: A tire is the outer part of a car wheel. It is usually made of rubber.
tire.sentence: The front tire on my bike needs changing.

tissue.definition: A piece of tissue is a sheet of paper that can absorb very well.
tissue.sentence: He used the tissue I gave him to blow his nose.

title.definition: The title of a book, movie, song, etc. is its name.
title.sentence: His title was Director of Science Education.

to.definition: To has no meaning. It is used with a bare infinitival clause.
to.sentence: It's important for you to understand.

today.definition: Today is the current day, the day that is happening now, the day between yesterday and tomorrow.
today.sentence: Today is the first day of the rest of your life.

together.definition: If you say that someone is together, you mean he or she is well organized and focused.
together.sentence: I really admire how together she is.

tone.sentence: He needed more practice to get proper control of the tone on his oboe.

tongue.definition: The part of the body that tastes food. It is pink or red and is inside the mouth.
tongue.sentence: He spoke in his native tongue.

tonight.definition: Tonight is the night that comes between today and tomorrow.
tonight.sentence: Tonight is when the party is scheduled.

too.definition: Too means to a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively.
too.sentence: You can't come in. You are too dirty.

tool.definition: A tool is an object that you use to do a specific job, such as a hammer.
tool.sentence: He is such a tool. He should think for himself, instead of doing everything they tell him to do.

tooth.definition: A tooth is a hard, white thing in your mouth. You use your teeth to chew food.

top.definition: The highest part of something; the upper part; the part people can put things on.
top.sentence: The top of the table is flat.

topic.definition: A topic is a general idea that someone is speaking (reading, thinking, etc.) about at a specific time.
topic.sentence: We were talking about my problems. Don't change the topic.

total.definition: A total is the final amount of something. It is a term used in math.

totally.definition: If something is totally true, it is 100% true.
totally.sentence: The class today was totally different from yesterday's class.

touch.definition: If you touch something, you feel it with your hand.
touch.sentence: Don't touch the oven -- it's hot and you will get a burn.

tough.definition: If something is tough, it is difficult, not easy.
tough.sentence: It's important to stay healthy when the going gets tough.

tour.definition: A tour is a planned walk, bus trip, or flight, to look at a particular place.
tour.sentence: Last year we took a wonderful tour to Rome.

tourism.definition: Tourism is the commercial organization and operation of visits to tourist destinations.
tourism.sentence: The tourism industry in China is booming.

tourist.definition: A tourist is a person who travels for pleasure, not for business.

tournament.definition: A tournament is a series of games until a winner is decided.
tournament.sentence: A lot of sports fans are looking forward to the college basketball championship tournament.

tower.definition: A tower is a tall building or structure.
tower.sentence: A tower of dust rose above the horizon.

town.sentence: She went to a town called Beaverton.

toy.definition: A toy is something that you can play with.

trace.definition: A trace of something is a very small amount, almost too small to find.
trace.sentence: No trace of the original material remains.

track.definition: A track is a line on the ground or in space that people, animals or vehicles follow.
track.sentence: He was far enough off the beaten track that nobody was liable to find him there.

trade.definition: When two people trade, one gives something to the other and the other gives something to the first one. They make an exchange. Sometimes money is one of the things.
trade.sentence: Trade in an old car for a new one.

tradition.definition: A tradition is something that has been done in the same way for a long time.
tradition.sentence: Despite a long tradition of education, there is still a lack of qualified teachers.

traditional.definition: If something is traditional, it has been done in the same way for a long time.
traditional.sentence: I learned traditional Japanese cooking from my grandmother.

traffic.definition: Traffic is the things that move along a path, especially cars on a road.
traffic.sentence: Traffic is slow at rush hour.

trail.definition: A trail is a way to get to a place, usually made of dirt and used by hikers or horse riders.
trail.sentence: That trail leads into the woods.

train.definition: A long vehicle with many cars that are joined together. A train runs on a track.
train.sentence: I took the train from Paris to Frankfurt.

transfer.definition: If you transfer (something), you move (it) to a different place.
transfer.sentence: If you learn to be organized in the classroom, then you can transfer that skill to your career later on.

transform.definition: When you transform something, you change it into a different thing totally.

transition.definition: A transition is a change from one place or situation to another.
transition.sentence: Diana has made the transition from girl to woman.

translate.definition: If you translate something from one language to another, you change the words and sentences into the other language.
translate.sentence: It's not enough to translate word for word.

transport.definition: Transport refers to how things are moved, or a system of transportation.
transport.sentence: I prefer my own means of transport.

transportation.definition: Transportation is the system or vehicles used to move people or things from one place to another.
transportation.sentence: In most of Canada, the main form of transportation is the family car.

travel.definition: When you travel, you visit some place; you go on a journey or adventure.

treat.definition: If you treat someone in a certain way, you act that way towards them.
treat.sentence: The doctor couldn't treat my finger until he saw the X-ray.

treatment.definition: A treatment is an action, usually by a doctor, to make somebody healthy.
treatment.sentence: The treatment that I have received since beginning this job has been terrible. My boss yells at me every day and nobody is friendly at all.

tree.definition: A tree is a tall plant of wood.
tree.sentence: I'm going to climb a tree.

trend.definition: A trend is a general movement or change in one direction.
trend.sentence: We expect the current upward trend in the use of our services to continue.

trial.definition: A trial is a meeting in court with a judge where two sides explain their positions and the judge or jury makes a decision.
trial.sentence: Jury selection in the trial began today.

trick.definition: To make someone think something that is not true.

trip.definition: A trip is a journey to a place.
trip.sentence: Let us go on a trip to John Doe Mountain. I have not been there in a while.

troop.definition: A troop is a soldier. This word is mostly used in the plural.

trouble.definition: Difficult or bad things happening; problems.
trouble.sentence: One trouble after another delayed the job.

truck.definition: A truck is a vehicle that is often used to carry or pull big loads.

true.definition: If something is true, it is correct or real, not imagined or made up.
true.sentence: She says she didn't take the money, but what she says is not true.

truly.definition: You use truly before an adjective to emphasize that something it has all the characteristics of that adjective.
truly.sentence: This has become a truly global business.

trust.definition: When you trust someone, you do not doubt them. You believe that someone is honest and will not cause harm. You believe you can rely on them.
trust.sentence: I trust all of my friends.

truth.definition: The truth is an idea which is correct or accepted as correct.
truth.sentence: Don't lie to me. Tell me the truth.

try.definition: If you try to do something, you make effort to do it.
try.sentence: It's OK. We'll try again tomorrow.

tube.definition: A tube is a long object with a hole from one end to the other. The ends may be closed or open.
tube.sentence: The high pressure forces the water through the tube.

tune.definition: A tune is a piece or part of music; a song or melody.
tune.sentence: Whistling a happy tune can chase the blues away.

turn.sentence: Walk down the street and turn left at the lights.

twin.definition: Twins are two people who were born at the same time from the same mother.
twin.sentence: We have twin beds in our room.

twist.definition: If you twist something, you turn one part of it in one direction and another part in the other direction at the same time.
twist.sentence: Twist the dough into a braid.

type.definition: A type is one thing or a group of things that are all members of a larger group because of some similarity.
type.sentence: I use the same type of camera at work.

typical.definition: If something is typical, it is normal, and not special. It's what you would expect.
typical.sentence: This rain isn't typical. We almost never get rain at this time of year.

typically.definition: If something typically happens, it happens in a common or expected manner.
